name: Hyderabadi Kheema
subtitle: minced mutton with peas, dry and heavily spiced, the weeknight standby

ingredients.note: goat mince; lamb works and is fattier

prepNotes: If the mince is frozen, thaw it fully and squeeze out the water. Wet mince boils instead of browning.
Chop the onions fine and evenly; coarse pieces stay crunchy in a dish that should be uniform.
Have the peas ready to go in at the twenty-minute mark, not at the start.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a kadhai and crackle the cumin seeds for 15 seconds.
Add the chopped onion and fry over medium heat for 10 minutes until golden brown and shrunk to a third of its volume.
steps.tip: Take the full ten minutes. Pale onion gives a thin, watery kheema.

steps.text: Stir in the ginger and garlic pastes and the green chillies and cook 1 minute until the raw smell lifts.
Add the mince and break it apart with the back of a spoon. Fry on high for 6-7 minutes until it is uniformly brown with no clumps.
steps.tip: Keep breaking it up in the first two minutes or it sets into lumps you cannot fix later.

steps.text: Add the turmeric, chilli powder, coriander powder, cumin powder and salt and fry 2 minutes.
Add the chopped tomatoes and cook 6-7 minutes until they melt down and oil beads at the edges of the pan.
Pour in the water, add the diced potato if using, cover and simmer on low for 15 minutes.
Add the peas, cover and cook 8 minutes more until the mince is tender and the liquid has almost gone.
Uncover and fry on medium for 4 minutes, stirring, until the kheema is dry and glistening rather than saucy.
steps.tip: Hyderabadi kheema is dry. Do not stop while there is still gravy in the pan.

steps.text: Stir in the garam masala, mint, coriander and lemon juice and rest 5 minutes before serving with roti or pav.

storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated and freezes well for 2 months. Reheat in a pan with 2 tbsp water over medium heat, breaking it up as it warms.
